references.text: The fourteenth day of the month and 'between the two evenings' are first mentioned in connection with the original Passover ordinance in Egypt.
Basic regulations for observing Passover, including that it must be kept at the appointed time with all its requirements.
Repeats the timing of Passover: the fourteenth day of the first month, between the two evenings.
Confirms the date of Passover as the fourteenth day of the first month.
Moses repeats the Passover regulations, emphasizing that Passover must be kept at the right time and in the right place.
Israel celebrates Passover on the fourteenth day of the month on the plains of Gilgal after entering the Promised Land.
King Josiah holds Passover in Jerusalem on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Those who had returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Ezekiel's prophecy about the future Passover observance on the fourteenth day of the first month.
